about: Benchmark atlas for Topic: benchmarks (Notion 3c65c17b0d0d811fb43fece56e40041a). One row per benchmark or benchmark version; versions are separate rows and never spliced. ev[0] is the headline reading behind the status. Other tabs may reuse ids and names (rows[].id, rows[].n, rows[].yr, rows[].fam, rows[].st).

exact: The answer is compared with a key: a letter, a number or a normalised string.
tests: Generated code is run against tests; it passes or fails.
exec: An environment's final state is inspected by a checker script (files, database, desktop).
judge: Another model grades the answer against a key or rubric.
pair: People compare two outputs and pick the better one; ratings come from the votes.
rubric: Experts score the output against criteria.
proof: A proof assistant (Lean, Isabelle) accepts or rejects a formal proof.
overlap: String overlap with a reference (F1, BLEU, chrF, ANLS).

none: Items are public and fixed; nothing stops them entering training data.
private: Some or all items are withheld and run only by the maintainer.
rolling: New items keep arriving with dates, so a model can be scored on items newer than its training data.
licensing: Items come from private code or data licensed for evaluation, never published.
interactive: Each run generates its own instances or an environment the model must explore; there is no answer list to leak.
transform: Existing items are rewritten at evaluation time so memorised surface cues disappear.

active: Still separates frontier models: the best score is well below the ceiling, or the set refreshes.
saturating: Top models cluster near the ceiling (roughly above 85 to 90%) but it still separates the tier below.
saturated: The top is at the ceiling or inside the noise of the answer key: no frontier signal left.
retired: Replaced by a successor or no longer reported on frontier model cards.
